transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sana Iqbal (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Redwood DevRel), Rahul Menon (Asteria CTO), Lisa Tran (Lead Engineer), Marcus Bell (Product), Ellen Zhao (SRE)

--- Auto summary (brief) ---
Jordan: quick sync to align on telemetry and SDK changes; check reproducer; next steps as action items.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): ok hi every-one thanks for joining, um let's do a quick round and then jump into the traces that Ellen sent, cool?
[00:00:08] Rahul (Asteria CTO): yeah thanks, Jordan. we saw that one of the flows in staging had pretty wide latency spikes, so we tried to capture full traces, i've shared the links in the doc.
[00:00:15] Lisa (Lead Engineer): hey sorry was on mute, the big problem for us is when the app does a bulk call to the invoke endpoint with tool-calls enabled, the responses sometimes come back malformed or missing the function-call payload.
[00:00:25] Sana (Redwood SE): got it, so that's the structured-output mismatch, we've seen similar where the function-calling layer and the SDK serializer disagree on empty args vs nulls.
[00:00:33] Marcus (Product): can you, um, remind us what versions of the SDK you were using? i think we were on the alpha node sdk on the staging cluster.
[00:00:40] Tom (DevRel): quick note — the alpha has a thin shim for streaming+function-calling; there's a newer patch that fixes a race in the serializer, we should make sure you're on that.
[00:00:48] Lisa: yep that's 0.9.4-alpha i think.
[00:00:52] Sana: okay we recommend 0.9.7-beta for the pilot, it contains the serializer fix and better backpressure handling for streaming sequences. i'll post links.
[00:01:05] Jordan: Ellen — can you walk us through the trace you captured? you had one with KV-prefetch flagged, right?
[00:01:11] Ellen (SRE): yeah so in the trace you can see requests 1011-1024 where the KV cache prefetch is triggered concurrently, sometimes the runtime returns a short-circuit value and the downstream function call receives incomplete context. i put a note at span 3.
[00:01:26] [00:01:30] Speaker 2: (unlabeled) there's a node that, uh, shows an error 502 at the pool layer but that might be the load balancer.
[00:01:35] Sana: okay, we're seeing two potential things: one is a race on the client side where prefetch kicks in mid-request, second is the server returning an early fallback when kv cache miss coincides with autoscaler spin up.
[00:01:50] Rahul: autoscaler... so would setting a higher min-instances on Dedicated or reserved pool avoid that?
[00:01:55] Jordan: yes that is one mitigation, if you bump min-instances you'll see fewer cold-start fallbacks, at cost of baseline spend. we'll put numbers in the sheet.
[00:02:04] [00:02:20] Lisa: another data point — we saw malformed payloads mostly when we use batched calls with mixed streaming and non-streaming routes, maybe an SDK boundary issue.
[00:02:28] Sana: that aligns with the serializer race i mentioned. workaround for now: disable batch combine for routes that use function-calling, or enable per-request header x-rdwd-force-serialize until you upgrade. both are temporary; we'll push a less invasive fix in the next patch.
[00:02:45] Marcus: ok can you quantify perf impact of disabling batch combine?
[00:02:50] Tom: rough estimate — for medium payloads it's 8-12% throughput loss but latency P95 improves for the problematic flows. i'll add a small table.
[00:03:00] [00:03:20] Jordan: i want to call out telemetry: Ellen's traces were missing a consistent trace_id across the SDK and server spans — looks like SDK instrumentation wasn't attaching the customer_trace header. are you using the built-in trace wrapper or a custom one?
[00:03:33] Ellen: we have a custom wrapper that enriches traces with request metadata. maybe it's dropping headers on redirects.
[00:03:40] Sana: that's probably it — redirects from our health checker strip non-standard headers in the node http client unless you set allow-external-headers true. small change but can cause trace id mismatch.
[00:03:52] Lisa: ok we can try that, will that require a restart?
[00:03:55] Sana: quick restart after env var flip. low risk.
[00:04:02] [00:04:30] Jordan: let's also standardize the telemetry fields we surface: we propose trace_id, route_name, model_variant, tokens_generated, function_calls_count, cache_hit boolean, and latency_ms as a standard set. does that work?
[00:04:45] Rahul: yes that should be fine. we also need user_id and request_origin for audit.
[00:04:50] Jordan: add those, good catch. we'll add user_id and request_origin to the sheet.
[00:05:00] [00:05:20] Tom: on the SDK side, i'll attach snippet examples for Node and Python in the follow-up. Node streaming example will show how to handle partial function-call JSON fragments so clients can reassemble safely.
[00:05:30] Lisa: the reassembly logic is the one we were worried about — do you have recommendations for a canonical parser?
[00:05:35] Sana: we recommend: 1) buffer until you see the closing bracket of the function-call JSON, 2) validate with the schema (we'll provide), 3) fall back to structured-cleaner API if validation fails. it's defensive but works across network jitter.
[00:05:50] [00:06:10] Marcus: is schema validation heavy on CPU? on mobile it's a concern.
[00:06:15] Sana: minor, JSON schema checks at the call boundary are tiny relative to model inference; the heavier part is reserializing nested tool payloads. we can show a benchmark.
[00:06:25] [00:06:40] Lisa: ok so two threads — SDK upgrade + telemetry header fix + run instrumented traces; and clamping batch combine for routes until patch lands.
[00:06:50] Jordan: yes and on the infra side, potentially bump min-instances for the reserved pool as a short-term mitigation. we'll show cost delta.
[00:07:10] [00:07:40] Ellen: quick Q — for the KV prefetch race, is there a runtime flag we can toggle to make prefetch synchronous?
[00:07:48] Sana: there's an internal flag prefetch.sync=true that makes the runtime await fetches before continuing; it's not enabled by default because it increases cold path latency, but we can enable it for your staging environment to test reproducibility.
[00:08:05] Rahul: let's enable it in staging and run the two traces — if it removes the missing context, that narrows it to the race.
[00:08:12] Jordan: agreed. add action item: Ellen to run with prefetch.sync and share results.
[00:08:20] [00:09:00] Tom: side note — we noticed a few places where V-P-C peering had MTU mismatch causing truncated headers, that also can silently drop custom headers used for tracing. Ellen, did you see any MTU logs?
[00:09:12] Ellen: yes we saw a few segmentation events yesterday, i'll pull those logs.
[00:09:18] Jordan: great, include that in the diagnostics bundle.
[00:09:30] [00:10:00] Lisa: on structured output stability, can you share the JSON Schema you plan to use? i want that to be part of our contract so our parser fails early.
[00:10:10] Sana: absolutely, we'll send schema v1 which includes required fields for function_call.name and function_call.arguments with types. note — the schema will accept both empty-object and null for absent args to avoid brittle failures.
[00:10:25] Marcus: how do we manage schema rollouts if you change the model prompt to add fields later?
[00:10:30] Jordan: plan is versioned schemas and compatibility checks at the gateway. we'll support opt-in strict mode for contracts. for the pilot, start non-strict then flip to strict once regression tests pass.
[00:10:50] [00:11:30] Rahul: timeline question — how long until the SDK patch and the prefetch flag test give us confidence to move this flow into staging?
[00:11:40] Sana: SDK patch is ready in beta; we can give you the snippet today. prefetch.sync test should be run in your staging cluster, results likely within 48 hours. so roughly 3 business days to confident baseline.
[00:11:55] Jordan: i'll put that in the next_steps.
[00:12:10] [00:12:40] Lisa: on observability, we wanted per-route token accounting — can the console show tokens per tool invocation?
[00:12:48] Tom: yes, Console can break down tokens by route and by tool call; we need the telemetry tag for function_calls_count to map. we'll map it automatically once tags are present.
[00:12:58] [00:13:20] Marcus: pricing question — if we keep min-instances up do we have a discount model for committed Dedicated?
[00:13:28] Jordan: yes with Dedicated you can commit a baseline and get lower per-token rates; we'll include a couple scenarios in the cost sheet for 24/7 baseline vs burstable.
[00:13:40] [00:14:00] Ellen: also to confirm — audit logs for structured-output are stored in the private audit trail? we need to ensure PII is not logged in plain text.
[00:14:08] Sana: audit logs capture metadata and request hashes by default, full payload logging is opt-in and redaction hooks exist. for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and field-level encryption.
[00:14:22] Rahul: perfect, that's in line with compliance.
[00:14:30] [00:14:50] Jordan: ok let's recap action items quickly — Jordan to send updated bench sheet, Sana to share SDK snippets and schema v1, Ellen to run prefetch.sync test and gather VPC MTU logs, Lisa to try header allow flip and do two instrumented traces.
[00:14:55] Lisa: yep that's correct.
[00:15:05] [00:15:30] Tom: i'll also add a note on disabling batch-combine per route and the rough perf numbers.
[00:15:40] Marcus: can we schedule a focused deep-dive if the prefetch test fails? maybe a SE-led troubleshooting session.
[00:15:47] Sana: yeah if the test fails we'll do an SE deep-dive with runtime logs, maybe include our runtime lead.
[00:15:55] Jordan: ok i'll put a tentative SE deep-dive slot for next Thursday if needed.
[00:16:10] [00:16:30] Rahul: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[00:16:35] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the updated spreadsheet. end.
